name: goldset_ga_ky
offsets: Character offsets into the UTF-8 decoded text of source_file. quote == text[start:end], verified on write.
definition: An obligation is a duty this document places on a utility: something it must do, must not do, must file, must report, or must do by a date.
labelling_rule: Labelled from the regulatory text alone. The annotator did not read the extraction code before labelling. Where a passage restates a duty created somewhere else (a prior order, a statute, a regulation) it is labelled false unless this document is the instrument that imposes it, and ambiguous is set true. Duties on Staff, on customers or on counsel are labelled false, because the definition scopes to utilities, and ambiguous is set true.
known_limits: One annotator. No second pass and no adjudication, so the ambiguous flag is one person's judgement of what another analyst might dispute, not a measured disagreement rate.

The Kentucky corpus here is intervenor testimony, errata and cover letters. It contains almost no operative obligations, so Kentucky passages skew negative. That is a property of the documents, not a sampling choice.

Passages were chosen to include hard cases on purpose. This set measures whether an extractor refuses to assert on recitals, denials, grants of authority and unadopted proposals. It is not a random sample and says nothing about recall over a whole document.
Source text comes from PDF and DOCX extraction. Some passages carry line numbers, running heads and irregular spacing. Offsets are into that raw text.

passages.quote: ORDERED FURTHER, that at least annually, the Company will update inputs to the minimum bill calculation.  Whenever the Company updates inputs to the minimum bill calculation, the Company shall notify Staff of the updates and shall provide Staff with an updated cost model.
passages.obligation_text: Georgia Power must refresh the inputs to its minimum bill calculation at least once a year, and each time it does so must tell Staff and hand over an updated cost model.
passages.why: Operative ORDERED clause. Names the actor, the act, the recipient and a recurring deadline.

passages.quote: ORDERED FURTHER, that the Company will file all executed large load contracts with the Commission as required by the Revision Approval Order.
passages.obligation_text: Georgia Power must file every executed large load contract with the Commission.
passages.why: Operative ORDERED clause imposing a filing duty. 'Will' rather than 'shall', but an ordered decretal paragraph is still a command.

passages.quote: the Company will file each such contract with the Commission at least thirty (30) days prior to execution of the contract. At the time of such filing, the Company will provide Commission Staff documentation demonstrating that the contract complies with the requirements of the Revision Approval Order.
passages.obligation_text: For any load of 100 MW or more, Georgia Power must file the contract with the Commission at least 30 days before signing it and, at the same time, give Staff papers showing the contract meets the Revision Approval Order.
passages.why: Second occurrence in the file, inside the ORDERED FURTHER section, so it is the adopted command rather than the Staff recommendation that repeats it verbatim earlier.

passages.quote: ORDERED FURTHER, that in implementing the tariffs and the large load contracting framework, the Company shall continue to exercise the discretion under the Rules and Regulations revisions in a manner designed to protect existing customers from bearing any of the costs of adding large load customers 100 MW or greater, including with respect to the minimum bill, termination, and collateral provisions established for these large load customers.
passages.obligation_text: When applying the tariffs and the large load contracting framework, Georgia Power must keep using its discretion so existing customers bear none of the cost of adding customers of 100 MW or more.
passages.why: A standard-of-conduct duty rather than a discrete task, but it is an ordered command on the utility and non-compliance is checkable.

passages.quote: ORDERED FURTHER, that a motion for reconsideration, rehearing, oral argument, or any other motion shall not stay the effective date of this Order unless otherwise ordered by the Commission.
passages.why: Hard negative. Contains 'shall not' but sets the procedural effect of the order, and puts no duty on anyone.

passages.quote: The Company shall file the complete contract and associated exhibits, attachments, terms and conditions on all new contracts within 30 days of execution.
passages.why: Hard negative, and the one I am least sure of. It sits under BACKGROUND, recounting a requirement the Commission imposed in its earlier 28 January 2025 order. The duty is real and live, so an analyst reading for 'what must we do' would flag it; but this document only recites it, and treating recitals as new obligations is how a docket ends up double-counting duties.

passages.quote: WHEREFORE IT IS ORDERED, that Staff’s recommendations on Georgia Power Company’s Revision to Rules and Regulations Tariff Compliance Filing, are hereby adopted.
passages.why: Hard negative. This clause is what makes the Staff recommendations binding, so it is the source of several obligations, yet it states no duty of its own. An analyst who labels by legal effect would call it true; I label by whether the passage itself says who must do what.

passages.quote: Georgia Power shall update the capacity need in the 2029-2031 All-Source Certification Proceeding in October 2025 with the B2026 Load Forecast, shall file additional Load Forecast updates in February 2027 with the B2027 Load Forecast, and as part of the 2028 IRP.
passages.obligation_text: Georgia Power must update the capacity need in the 2029-2031 All-Source Certification Proceeding in October 2025 using the B2026 load forecast, file further load forecast updates in February 2027 using the B2027 forecast, and file updates again in the 2028 IRP.
passages.why: Three dated filing duties in one sentence. First occurrence is the order body; the attached Stipulation repeats it later.

passages.quote: The Company will provide semi-annual reports on the status of 111 GHG Rule compliance starting with the semi-annual period ending December 31, 2025, with the report to be submitted by March 31 and September 30 of each year.
passages.obligation_text: Georgia Power must file semi-annual reports on its compliance with the 111 GHG Rule, starting with the period ending 31 December 2025, due 31 March and 30 September each year.
passages.why: Named reports, a start period and two fixed dates a year.

passages.quote: Georgia Power shall adopt a formal process to evaluate Grid Enhancing Technologies ("GETs") as potential solutions for all major Georgia Power transmission projects and will include in the 2028 IRP a report on the planning assumptions, criteria, and outcomes associated with its GETs evaluations.
passages.obligation_text: Georgia Power must set up a formal process for weighing Grid Enhancing Technologies on all major transmission projects and must report on that process and its outcomes in the 2028 IRP.
passages.why: A duty to build a process plus a duty to report on it in a named future filing.

passages.quote: The Company shall issue an All-Source RFP for capacity needs in 2032-2033 in the first quarter of 2026.
passages.obligation_text: Georgia Power must issue an All-Source RFP for 2032-2033 capacity needs during the first quarter of 2026.
passages.why: Single act with a fixed window.

passages.quote: In addition, the Company will continue to file the ECS annually with the Commission no later than March 31 of each year.
passages.obligation_text: Georgia Power must keep filing its Environmental Compliance Strategy with the Commission every year, by 31 March.
passages.why: 'Continue to file' carries the duty forward rather than creating it fresh, but the sentence still states the act, the recipient and the deadline.

passages.quote: The request to develop, own, and operate incremental capacity at Plant Goat Rock Units 3-6 shall not be approved at this time.
passages.why: Hard negative. 'Shall not be approved' is a refusal of relief, not a duty. Nothing is required of anyone; a request is simply denied.

passages.quote: The Company shall be authorized to seek certification of up to 8,500 MW of capacity from the 2029-2031 All Source Capacity RFP.
passages.why: Hard negative. 'Shall be authorized' grants permission with a ceiling. Georgia Power may seek certification; nothing says it must.

passages.quote: Should the 111 GHG Rule repeal be finalized by EPA and the Company's compliance preparations conclude, the semi-annual reports shall no longer be required.
passages.why: Hard negative, and genuinely contestable. The sentence contains 'shall' and 'required' but its effect is to end a reporting duty once a condition is met. I read it as a sunset clause; an analyst who treats the whole reporting paragraph as one obligation would fold this in rather than label it separately.

passages.quote: Georgia Power countered by noting that it had both proposed the 0.75% DSM savings target and supported that same target throughout the 2025 IRP proceeding.
passages.why: Recital of a party's argument in the procedural history. Reports what Georgia Power said, not what it must do.

passages.quote:
The Company will provide each participating customer with a credit on the customer’s monthly electric bill in 
exchange for the Company’s use of the customer’s DER for the economic dispatch of electric energy to the 
electric grid.
passages.obligation_text: Under the DCO-1 tariff, Georgia Power must give each participating customer a bill credit in return for using that customer's distributed energy resource for economic dispatch.
passages.why: A filed and approved tariff binds the utility, so I read this as a duty owed to participating customers. But it sits under PRICING METHODOLOGY and reads as a description of how the programme works, so an analyst could fairly call it descriptive rather than obligatory.

passages.quote:
Participating customers must enter a written DER Customer-Owned Agreement (DCO Agreement) with the 
Company,  referencing  this  schedule.
passages.why: Hard negative under the rule that an obligation binds the utility. This is a real duty, plainly worded with 'must', but it falls on customers. An analyst working from a wider definition of obligation would label it true, which is exactly why it belongs in the set.

passages.quote:
hereby files an original and fifteen (15) copies of its Quarterly Large Load Economic Development 
Report for the period ending September 30, 2025.
passages.why: Hard negative. This is a utility reporting that it has discharged a duty, not the creation of one. It names the utility, an act, a count and a date, so it reads like an obligation; the tense is what gives it away. Contestable because the underlying quarterly-report duty is real and is referenced in the same letter.

passages.quote:
The utility shall provide a reconciliation of the rate base and capital used to determine its
revenue requirements.
passages.obligation_text: Kentucky Utilities must file a reconciliation of the rate base and the capital used to set its revenue requirement.
passages.why: This is 807 KAR 5:001 Section 16(6)(f), a filing requirement the utility had to meet in this very case, so the duty is live and on the utility. It is contestable because the passage appears inside an intervenor's exhibit reproducing the requirement, not in the utility's own filing or in an order.

passages.quote:
KRS 278.264(1)  states specifically  that, “Prior to  retiring an  electric

 2           generating unit, a utility shall apply to the commission for an order approving the

 3           retirement, and  shall  give  the commission  thirty  (30) days  notice  of  the

 4           application.”
passages.why: The hardest call in this set. The quoted statute plainly binds utilities, but the passage is an intervenor witness quoting law to argue that the Company has not followed it. Treating quoted statute as an obligation of this docket would put duties on a rate case that the rate case never imposed. I label it false on that reasoning and concede an analyst could go the other way.

passages.quote:
I recommend that the Commission reject the Companies’ proposals to include the

 6         amounts in accounts 128 Prepaid Pension, 182 Regulatory Asset – FAS 158

 7          Pension, and 184 Pension Clearing Account in rate base and subtract the amounts

 8            in accounts 228.3 Accumulated Provision for Post Retirement Benefits and 254

 9          Regulatory  Liability – Postretirement from  rate base for the reasons  that  I

10           previously described.
passages.why: Hard negative. A witness recommendation the Commission has not acted on. If the Commission adopts it, the resulting order creates the obligation; the testimony does not.

passages.quote:
Walmart recommends that the Commission require the Company to work

 2                        with interested stakeholders to develop a new EV rate specifically for

 3                          public-facing Direct Current Fast Chargers ("DCFC") and to either seek

 4                     Commission approval of such rate or provide an update on the stakeholder

 5                         process within six months following the issuance of a Final Order in this

 6                           case.
passages.why: Hard negative, and a deliberate trap: 'recommends that the Commission require the Company to' contains the whole grammar of an obligation and a six-month deadline, yet nothing has been required of anyone. It is an intervenor's ask.

passages.quote: Page 20, Line 14: Replace "intraclass" with "interclass".
passages.why: An errata correction to a witness's own testimony. Imperative in form, but it changes a document; it places no duty on the utility.

passages.quote:
In accordance with 807 KAR 5:001 § 8, Counsel certifies that the
electronically filed documents are a true representation of the documents being emailed to the
parties of record, and that no party has been excused from participation by electronic service.
passages.why: Counsel certifying that a service rule was met. It cites the rule that creates the duty and asserts the duty was discharged, so it is a statement of past compliance. Contestable because the certification requirement itself is an obligation, and it falls on counsel for an intervenor, not on a utility.
